what_it_contains: Two provisional category scores. Zero is the mean of the reference-standardized components; positive is better. See basket and coverage columns.
One row per country/economy and year, with a separate labeled column for each observed indicator.
Annual outcomes, original indicators and fixed-basket living-standard sensitivity used in the expanded models.
World Bank country-year panel joined to reviewed V-Dem identifiers. Happiness is deliberately excluded because its observations cover multiple years.
Compares annual relative scores with scores anchored to the 2010 mean and standard deviation. Observation count refers to the 2010 indicator reference.
Descriptive freedom basket: civil liberties, expression and association. All three are required. It shares ingredients with democracy and cannot independently test democracy effects.
Non-overlapping happiness reporting windows. Predictors precede the full window, not just its ending year.
Observed 0-10 life-evaluation averages for explicitly labeled multi-year periods. Rank is separate. Early period start is left unassigned.
Official income group in force on July 1 of each observation year. Fiscal year and underlying GNI data year are separate. Starred retrospective classifications are excluded.
Six verified census Gini values for two household populations and 2011/2016/2021. Printed page 98, PDF page 110; separate local case study.
Original IMF fields plus general-government investment / same-source nominal GDP. May 2021 vintage ends in 2019. Narrow fiscal measure, not total intervention.
One row per country/economy, year and indicator. Values retain original units; blank means missing.
Complete observations actually used in living-standard models. Predictors refer to exactly the preceding calendar year.
Periodic ownership-regulation scores with actual legal-reference dates. Wave names are not assumed to be the observation year. No annual filling.
Annual growth, living and gender outcomes with exact preceding-year ownership and other predictors. SWIID outcomes are excluded from regression.
Observed national PIP survey outcomes with preceding-year ownership, separate welfare types and comparable-spell metadata.
Strictly nationally labeled survey records, without interpolation. Income and consumption remain distinct.
Pinned PIP survey records with welfare concept, geography, comparability spell and unit conversions. Includes non-national records for inspection.
Same observed data restricted to the 11 selected cases. Hong Kong is a separately reported economy.
Annual outcomes with exact preceding-year public investment and institutional predictors. Investment vintage ends in 2019.
Official Singapore Gini definitions, populations, equivalence scales and tax treatments. A separate local case study, never spliced into PIP.
Observed national surveys joined to preceding-year predictors, with comparable-spell identifiers retained. Gaps are not filled.
Raw values plus transformed values, annual z-scores and percentiles. At least 100 valid reference economies are required for scoring.
Expert-assessed ownership/direct control, original V-Dem values, reversed 0-4 expected scale and uncertainty. Not an asset percentage or a welfare score.
Published SWIID standardized/model-based disposable and market income estimates. Provider uncertainty retained; not direct survey data or regression-ready validated draws.
Same-vintage UNDP Gender Inequality Index, 1990-2023. Lower raw values mean less inequality; higher relative z means less relative disadvantage. Hong Kong remains missing.
Audited V-Dem v16 country-year indices, original IDs and uncertainty. Historical raw values are retained; modern benchmarking begins in 2000.
V-Dem raw values and annual scores using at least 100 matched reference economies. Provider bounds are not labeled as 95 percent intervals.
Coverage by V-Dem index/year and happiness reporting period. Observed counts refer to matched economies, not individual survey respondents.
Same economies with observed values in all 25 years for each indicator. Balanced selection can exclude data-poor economies and is not a representative global sample.
Accepted, limited and unavailable candidate sources, including dependent sources and the failed WIID public download.
Observed values for selected cases in 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020 and 2024. A missing requested year remains blank.
Missing share over all requested years 1965-2025 for each selected case and indicator.
Any failed collection requests in the latest pipeline run; a header-only file means no failures.
Number of jointly observed country-year pairs behind each correlation.
Pairwise correlations from country-year observations since 2000. Diagonal equals 1. This is association, not causation.
Coverage counts by indicator and year. Missing share uses the full reference catalog as denominator.
Raw annual means for economies classified as high income today. This is not historical high-income membership. Observation count is economies.
Exploratory stage alignment to Singapore 2000 PPP income, requiring a sustained three-year threshold and at most 10 percent initial overshoot. Earliest-observation matches are left-censored.
Expanded model estimates and country-clustered 95 percent confidence intervals. Outcome units differ, so coefficients across outcomes are not directly comparable.
Sample size, time window and basic model diagnostics. All models remain exploratory associations.
Country/economy, outcome year and predictor year for every expanded model sample.
Observed-outcome rows compared with complete-case model rows. Differences show sample loss from missing predictors.
Collinearity and residual predictor variation after removing each model fixed-effect structure.
New narrow-investment and social-survey model estimates, with country-clustered 95 percent confidence intervals and explicit outcome concepts.
Model sample, window, fixed-effect structure, influence and heteroskedasticity diagnostics. Exploratory, not causal validation.
Exact country/economy-year membership of each new model; paired baseline/investment models use identical rows.
Sample losses, comparability-block counts, sample gates and estimation status for the new models.
Collinearity and remaining predictor variation after each model fixed-effect structure.
Relative scores for the 11 cases. Annual categories refer to 2024; life evaluation refers to 2022-2024. Social scores are unavailable.
Plain-language status for all five outcome categories: available data, current modeling and unresolved limits.
Annual gender-index reference counts and raw mean/SD; relative scores require at least 100 observed economies.
Annual indicator benchmarks. Raw statistics retain original units; transformed statistics reflect the stated transformation.
Raw annual indicator means and standard deviations using historical income groups or current geographic regions. Counts show membership and observed coverage; no peer z-scores are assumed.
All 11 cases, showing usable investment years, OECD assessment dates, PIP concept/coverage and local source status.
Simple source-by-source decisions: what is usable, what question it measures and what remains unresolved.
Sensitivity for complete baskets only. Compares full-category score with a score omitting the named indicator.
Main country/year-effect ownership coefficients for growth, living standards and gender inequality; units differ by outcome.
Sample size, model fit, heteroskedasticity and influence diagnostics. These do not establish causality.
Average annual observed-economy count and missing share across 2000-2025, including incomplete recent reporting.
Ownership/direct-control association models. Country-clustered 95 percent intervals are conditional on point predictor estimates.
Sample, time window, influence and heteroskedasticity diagnostics for new ownership models.
Exact model sample membership and predictor years; baseline and main ownership specification share identical rows.
Model sample gates and estimation status, including observed-survey welfare concepts.
Predictor collinearity and remaining variation after removing the model fixed effects.
All 11 cases with source-specific last years; different last years are not silently treated as simultaneous comparisons.
Observed provider variation, distinct values and adjacent-year changes. Repeated scores do not prove unchanged real policy.
Selected-case provisional scores for 2015-2025. Use same-year comparisons and inspect changing basket composition.
Number of the 11 selected cases with a usable category score in each year.
Main same-sample investment coefficients with readable outcome units. Each coefficient refers to +1 percentage point of GDP in prior-year government investment.
Economies with usable same-source nominal investment/GDP ratios, by year.
Living-standard model estimates and 95 percent country-clustered confidence intervals. Observation count is country-year rows.
Singapore compared with its historical income group and current geographic region, in original indicator units. Positive differences are not always better.
Survey-year reference means, separating income and consumption. These are raw survey comparisons, not a global composite.
Diagnostic-only format/summary discrepancies. Trial division is not an accepted unit conversion. Draw-based regression is explicitly withheld.
All 11 cases in the latest common SWIID year, 2016. Provider-modeled income summaries with approximate uncertainty; no mixed latest years.
Unweighted same-year reference statistics of published standardized estimates, with observed economy count; not a direct-survey population mean.
Annual means, standard deviations and coverage for the matched modern V-Dem reference population.
Same-year candidate WDI/PIP Gini comparisons. Different vintages or welfare concepts can produce different values; no automatic substitution.
Categories with no approved composite score yet. No missing score is replaced with zero.
Standard deviation after subtracting each economy mean; predictor units are unchanged.
